atoms.text: There are many types of flood defences in place to protect people and the landscape. There are two types of flood defences in England: hard and soft.

Types of hard defences include: dams, barriers, and pumping stations. The aim of hard flood defences is to control the water and divert it downstream so that it does not cause damage. The first self-closing barrier opened in Cumbria in 2012 after years of bad flooding in 2005 and 2009. As a result of these floods, many people had to evacuate their homes.

Soft flood defences are a more sustainable approach to managing flooding. Flood warnings are often issued by the environmental agency. This means that people have time to protect their properties and save their possessions. Ecological flooding means that some parts of the river are allowed to flood naturally. This means that towns which are close to the river are protected, and new freshwater habitats can form.
